reason: R0 is part of the bias/common-mode linkage between IB2 and IB1 through VCM1; removing it typically leaves the main output branches (NMOS sinks M4/M5 with PMOS loads M6/M7) still functional. Caveat: IB2/IB1 coupling (and any intended common-mode stabilization) is reduced, so output common-mode and matching may drift.
impact_estimate: Low (core amplification path remains; common-mode/bias tracking degrades)

reason: R1 completes the IB2–VCM1–IB1 resistive network; deleting it usually doesn’t break signal conduction from the VB1/VB2-controlled devices to VOUT1/VOUT2. Caveat: if IB1 is expected to be generated/trimmed via VCM1, removing R1 can shift bias currents and reduce CMRR.

M8 is a VB3-biased PMOS current source setting the bias node net027 for the pull-up device M6; if net027 (or the pull-up current) is provided by another bias source, M8 can be removed without breaking the basic output branch operation. Caveat: without an alternate bias, M6 current becomes undefined, reducing gain and shifting VOUT1 DC level.
impact_estimate: Low-to-moderate (bias/gain changes unless net027 is biased elsewhere)
